# A hotel bill of 45.00 USD paid out of the CAD bank for 63.23 CAD.
#
# The USD split states both amounts, 45.00 USD and a value of 63.23 CAD, and
# `share_price: "6323/4500"`, the price those two give. The tests replace that
# price with one the two amounts do not give. An expense holds no cost basis,
# so the transaction can be read again with `--strategy update`.
#
# What this fixture produces: one CAD transaction, Expenses:Travel USD
# +45.00 USD valued 63.23 CAD against Assets:Bank -63.23 CAD.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_a_price_beside_two_amounts_is_the_one_they_give.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Travel USD
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

2026-01-10 * "Hotel in USD"
	guid: "a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1a1"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Expenses:Travel USD 45.00 USD
		guid: "b1b1b1b1b1b1b1b1b1b1b1b1b1b1b1b1"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "6323/4500"
		value: "63.23"
	Assets:Bank -63.23 CAD
		guid: "c1c1c1c1c1c1c1c1c1c1c1c1c1c1c1c1"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
		value: "-63.23"
